item.text:
When an HTTPX `Client` follows a redirect, it **retains `Authorization` if the destination has the same origin**: the same scheme, host, and effective port. `_same_origin` uses `_port_or_default`, so an omitted HTTP port counts as 80 and an omitted HTTPS port as 443. [`_same_origin` and `_port_or_default`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/httpx/_client.py#L72-L85); [`test_same_domain_redirect`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/tests/client/test_redirects.py#L261-L267).

For a different origin, `BaseClient._redirect_headers` removes `Authorization`, including on a host change, port change, or HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect. **The exception is a direct HTTP-to-HTTPS upgrade on the same host, from effective port 80 to 443**; `_is_https_redirect` allows the header to remain. [`_redirect_headers`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/httpx/_client.py#L505-L517); [`_is_https_redirect`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/httpx/_client.py#L58-L69).

The tests confirm that cross-domain redirects remove the header even when the destination is HTTPS, while a same-host HTTP-to-HTTPS redirect retains it. [`cross-domain tests`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/tests/client/test_redirects.py#L238-L259); [`HTTP-to-HTTPS test`](https://github.com/encode/httpx/blob/master/tests/client/test_redirects.py#L269-L275).
